summary: A prefabricated cast-iron tower of 1851 on Newfoundland's southern tip, kept by three generations of the Hewitt family until 1996.

notes_for_editor: Mostly rests on one copyrighted secondary source (Lighthousefriends), paraphrased; capepine.com history page returned 403 and Parks Canada NHS page was empty. Lighthousefriends gives de-staffing 1996 and Valentine Hewitt to 1973 but the Peter Myrick/Michael Myrick sequence is garbled (Michael from 1973, Peter 1990-96, Tom Finlay undated). It also says 1879 for Costello's accident (four years after 1875); 'Michael Myrick' as fog-alarm keeper may be a different person. Marvale: 1923-24 report lists the sinking under a Marine department ship's log (dates May 25 to June 14, year inferred); the distress message is dated 21 May 1923. Lucile M. Schnare year unconfirmed (OCR table, matched by position). Light-list page cache was truncated so no characteristic cited. Lens figures (17 m tower, 92 m focal plane) from LF; record has 18 m and 95.7 m. Fact-check: Lucile M. Schnare entry names a second vessel (OCR 'Wartentels', London) matched by position; finding 'No one to blame, collision unavoidable'. Removed 'still working' (no cited source).
